builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Hierarchical Low-Rank Reparameterization for Parameter-Efficient
summary: Replaces the standard trainable parameter matrices of PEFT adapters (LoRA, DoRA, MoSA, RaSA) with a recursive low-rank factorization that reorganizes them into approximately square matrices and decomposes them level by level. Cost is additional implementation complexity and retraining of the factorization; inference cost of the deployed adapter is unchanged or lower given fewer parameters. Can fail on tasks or model families not covered by the evaluations (only commonsense reasoning and GSM8K on 7-8B models were tested), and the recursive factorization may underperform when the target parameter budget is not extremely tight or when adapter redundancy is low.
rationale: The method is directly applicable to single-GPU PEFT workflows and reduces already-small adapter sizes further, but gains are demonstrated only on narrow benchmarks and require per-workload validation before production adoption.
technique: Hierarchical low-rank reparameterization of PEFT adapters

claims.statement: Replaces the standard trainable parameter matrices of PEFT adapters (LoRA, DoRA, MoSA, RaSA) with a recursive low-rank factorization that reorganizes them into approximately square matrices and decomposes them level by level. Cost is additional implementation complexity and retraining of the factorization; inference cost of the deployed adapter is unchanged or lower given fewer parameters. Can fail on tasks or model families not covered by the evaluations (only commonsense reasoning and GSM8K on 7-8B models were tested), and the recursive factorization may underperform when the target parameter budget is not extremely tight or when adapter redundancy is low.

Trainable-parameter count of LoRA/DoRA/MoSA/RaSA can be compressed by approximately an order of magnitude while maintaining or surpassing baseline average accuracy across eight commonsense reasoning benchmarks on LLaMA-3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-7B.
